A git version tag must consist of an optional lowercase 'v' prefix followed by a version number. The version number must have at least one and at most three dot-separated numeric components. The first component must not have a leading zero unless it is exactly '0'. Each subsequent component, if present, may be a single '0' or a number without leading zeros. After the numeric version, an optional pre-release part may follow, which must begin with a hyphen and consist of one or more dot-separated identifiers. Each identifier may contain only ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens, and must not be empty. No build metadata is allowed.
Our release schedule uses calendar versioning: a release identifier is a four-digit year, a dot, and a two-digit month (01 through 12). The month must always be two digits.

In our package manager configuration, we need to validate version range expressions. A valid range is a caret (^) or tilde (~) followed by a semantic version number, which has three numeric parts separated by dots. Each part must be a non-negative integer without leading zeros unless the number is exactly zero.
Match a ULID: 26 characters from Crockford's Base32 alphabet (digits 0-9 and letters A-Z excluding I, L, O, and U), case-insensitive.
git commit hash: exactly 7 or 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters

We need to validate a user-supplied identifier that is a version 4 UUID. It must be the standard 36-character hyphenated form with lowercase hexadecimal digits, and the version and variant nibbles must be exactly 4 and one of 8, 9, a, or b respectively.
even-length lowercase hexadecimal string

Validate a passphrase consisting of at least four words. Each word is made of letters (a-z, A-Z) or digits (0-9) only, and words are separated by exactly one space. The passphrase must not start or end with a space.

Match a euro price written in French convention: digits grouped in threes with a single space as the thousands separator, an optional fractional part of one or two decimal digits introduced by a comma, and the euro sign at the end after a space. The space before the euro sign is required.

Our accounting export writes credit balances as negative amounts, so the ledger team needs the amount field validated: a negative figure is wrapped in a pair of parentheses with no space inside them, and the figure itself has whole units grouped in threes by commas, an optional decimal part after a period, and an optional leading dollar sign directly attached to the first digit group. Positive amounts are handled elsewhere, so only these parenthesized amounts are accepted here; no currency checksum is verified.

The string must be a price consisting of an integer part of one or more digits, optionally digit-grouped with commas but only where each group after the first has exactly three digits, followed by a decimal point and exactly two digits. No currency symbol or sign is allowed.

Identifier must be either snake_case or SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE:
- Only ASCII letters, digits and underscores are allowed.
- It must not start with a digit and must not consist solely of digits.
- It must not start or end with an underscore, and it must not contain two or more consecutive underscores.
- Either all letters are lowercase with at least one underscore present, or all letters are uppercase with at least one underscore present.

Match a name that is either snake_case or SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. It may contain letters, digits and underscores, but it cannot start or end with an underscore and cannot have two underscores in a row. All letters must be lowercase if it is snake_case, or all uppercase if it is screaming snake case. At least one underscore is required.

In the loyalty program, a member's point balance is stored as a whole number written without any separators. Members who have been flagged as at-risk must not have balances that end in the digit seven, since that value is reserved for a promotional code collision. A valid balance is a non-negative integer of up to nine digits that does not end in seven.

Validate a snake_case identifier. Rules:
- Either all lowercase letters with underscores, or all uppercase letters with underscores (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).
- Words are separated by single underscores.
- Must contain at least two words.
- No digits, no leading/trailing underscores, no double underscores.
kebab-case css class name

In the accounts admin panel we show an internal project code. The code always starts with an uppercase letter, followed by any mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits and underscores, but it must not be completely uppercase: at least one lowercase letter must be present after the first character, otherwise the code is considered an external one and must be rejected.

Our invoicing system needs to validate an order quantity that is a whole number, may optionally be preceded by a minus sign, and must not end in the digit 7 because quantities ending in 7 are reserved for backorders.

Our users can enter a short note. The field must accept between one and three lines of text. Each line may contain any characters except line breaks. The entire note must not end with a line break (i.e., a trailing newline is not allowed). The note must not be empty.

Match a multi-line string in which every line contains a number, optionally preceded by a minus sign, and nothing else. Lines are separated by newline characters, there must be at least one line, and the input must not end with a newline.
A string of digits (no sign, no decimal point) that does not end with the digit 7. At least one digit is required.

A git branch name following this convention: it starts with one of the prefixes feature/, bugfix/, hotfix/, or release/ followed by a slash, then a short description in lowercase consisting of alphanumeric words separated by single hyphens. No leading or trailing hyphens and no consecutive hyphens.

A valid HTTP status line must be a string that starts with 'HTTP/', followed by a version consisting of a single digit, a dot, and another single digit, then a space, then a three‑digit status code. The status code must be exactly three digits, and its first digit must be either '4' or '5'. The string must end immediately after the status code; no trailing spaces or characters are allowed. The entire match is case‑sensitive, so 'http/' is invalid.

Our error tracking system expects log lines that contain an error code. An error code is the letter 'E' followed by exactly three digits, and it must appear as a standalone token: it must be preceded by a start-of-string or a non-word character, and followed by an end-of-string or a non-word character. For example, 'E123' is valid, but 'FE123' or 'E1234' should not be considered valid error codes.

Matches a Unix absolute path. Rules: 1. Must start with a forward slash /. 2. Must not contain any null bytes or backslashes. 3. Must not contain consecutive slashes (//) except when the path is exactly / (the root). 4. May contain alphanumeric characters, dots, hyphens, underscores, and spaces, but each path component cannot be empty. 5. May end with a trailing slash (which is optional), except when the path is just /.

Match a file name that is exactly one image file with a JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, or SVG extension, with the extension written in lowercase. The part before the dot must be at least one character long and may not contain a path separator or a dot.

A valid email address that does not belong to a free webmail domain. The email must have a local part of one or more characters that are letters, digits, or any of these special characters: . _ % + -. The local part cannot start or end with a dot, and cannot have two consecutive dots. The domain must have at least two labels separated by dots, each label consisting of letters, digits, or hyphens, and cannot start or end with a hyphen. The top-level domain must be at least two letters. The domain must not be exactly 'gmail.com', 'yahoo.com', 'hotmail.com', or 'outlook.com', case-insensitive.

A JavaScript variable name is valid when it is a sequence of letters, digits, dollar signs or underscores that does not start with a digit, and it is not one of the reserved words var, let, const, class or function.
